name: Easy Event CAD
author: easyeventcad

sections.description:
Easy Event CAD lets party and tent rental companies’ customers lay out
their event to scale: tents, tables, chairs, dance floors and more, with a
pull sheet and a quote request at the end. This plugin puts your company’s
planner on your WordPress site.

The plugin is a thin wrapper. It contains no planning logic of its own: it
outputs the same embed snippet you could copy by hand from your Easy Event
CAD account (Settings, then Embed & branding), using the company code and
display settings you save here. The planner itself is served by Easy Event
CAD, so it stays up to date without plugin updates.

A launcher card (a button or image that opens the planner full screen) is
the default and fits anywhere, even a sidebar. Inline mode puts the planner
straight into a page. You can also show up to two saved example layouts so
visitors see a real starting plan before they click in.

Using the shortcode or block also avoids a common problem: some hosting
security filters (for example ModSecurity) refuse to save or show a page
that contains a pasted script tag. With the plugin, the page only stores
[easyeventcad].

Features

  • Settings page to store your company code, default mode (Launcher, Inline,
    or Popup), default height, launcher card copy/image, and up to two seeded
    plan previews.
  • A real, executing live preview on the Settings page — see your actual
    current configuration render before you use it anywhere.
  • [easyeventcad] shortcode, with optional per-placement overrides:
    [easyeventcad mode=”launcher” launcher_heading=”Design Your Tent”].
  • “Easy Event CAD Planner” block for the block editor (Gutenberg), with the
    same settings available in the block sidebar.
  • No API keys, tokens, or secrets are ever stored — your company code is
    public information (it’s the same slug in your shareable planner link).

Requirements

  • An Easy Event CAD account (https://easyeventcad.com). Your company code
    is shown in your account under Settings, Embed & branding, and is the
    last part of your hosted planner link, for example
    app.easyeventcad.com/d/your-company.
  • If you use the Allowed websites list in your Easy Event CAD account, add
    your WordPress site’s address to it, or the browser will not show the
    planner.

External services

This plugin connects to Easy Event CAD (https://easyeventcad.com), a hosted
event-layout service run by Easy Event CAD LLC. It is needed to show the
planner; without it the plugin does nothing.

  • What is loaded: on any page where you place the shortcode or block (and
    on the plugin’s Settings page, for the live preview), the visitor’s
    browser loads the planner script embed.js and the planner itself from
    your configured planner host (by default https://app.easyeventcad.com).
  • What is sent: your company code and display settings, the address of the
    page the planner sits on, and the usual information any browser sends
    with a web request (such as IP address and browser type). Anything the
    visitor enters in the planner (event details, and their name, email and
    phone if they ask for a quote) is sent to Easy Event CAD and shared with
    your rental company. The planner also records anonymous usage events
    (for example, that it was opened).
  • Nothing is sent from your WordPress server; the plugin stores only your
    settings, in one WordPress option.

Terms of Service: https://easyeventcad.com/legal/terms
Privacy Policy: https://easyeventcad.com/legal/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the easy-event-cad folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install
    the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings → Easy Event CAD and enter your company code (shown in
    your Easy Event CAD account under Settings, Embed & branding).
  4. Add [easyeventcad] to any post/page, or add the “Easy Event CAD
    Planner” block.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin store any of my customers’ data?

No. All planning happens inside the embedded iframe, served entirely by
Easy Event CAD. This plugin only stores your company code and display
preferences (mode, height, button label) as a single WordPress option.
Nothing about your site visitors passes through WordPress. See “External
services” above for what the planner sends to Easy Event CAD.

Can I embed more than one planner (different modes) on the same site?

Yes — the shortcode and block both accept per-placement mode, height,
and launcher-copy overrides, so one page can be a launcher card and another
can be forced inline, independent of your saved default.

What is “Launcher” mode, and why is it the default?

A launcher is a small card (a button, or your own image) that opens the
full planner in a full-screen overlay when clicked. It’s the default
because it works in any placement — a sidebar, a footer widget, a narrow
column. Inline mode renders the planner directly in the page at every
placement size, phones included (since v2.1.0): the embedded planner is
the guided question flow, which is built for small screens — tablets get
full editing, phones get the interview plus a view-only plan with a quote
button. Pick Inline for a dedicated planner page, Launcher for a card
placed among other content.

Can I show a real starting layout before a visitor clicks in?

Yes — configure up to two “seed” plan IDs (UUIDs from your Easy Event CAD
account) in Settings, or per-placement via the shortcode/block. With one
seed configured, the launcher opens straight into that plan; with two, the
visitor sees a small picker plus a “start blank” option. A missing, revoked,
or invalid seed silently falls back to a blank planner — it never shows an
error.

The planner doesn’t load — just a blank space or a missing button.

Two different notes cover the two ways this happens. If the planner
iframe loaded but stays blank for about 12 seconds, your WordPress domain
probably isn’t on your Allowed websites list (Settings, Embed & branding
in your Easy Event CAD account; leave the list empty to allow any site, or
add your address, such as https://www.your-site.com); a note saying so
appears under the frame. If nothing appears at all — no iframe, no card — the planner
script itself never ran: a network firewall or DNS filter blocking the
planner domain, or a browser extension blocking third-party scripts.
Since v2.1.0 the placement then shows a note plus a direct link that opens
the hosted planner in a new tab. On a managed office network, ask IT to
allow the planner host you configured under Settings → Easy Event CAD
(by default app.easyeventcad.com).
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • Changed: the planner’s script tags are now built with WordPress’s own
    wp_get_script_tag() and wp_get_inline_script_tag(), so they follow
    your site’s script filters (for example a Content Security Policy nonce).
    The planner looks and works the same.
  • Changed: readme for the WordPress.org plugin directory, including an
    “External services” section, and the plugin and author links now point
    at easyeventcad.com.

2.1.0

  • Changed: Inline mode now always renders the planner inline — at every
    placement size, phones included. The app’s embedded planner is the
    guided question flow (since the app-side 2026-08-24 cutover), which is
    designed for small screens: tablets get full editing, phones get the
    interview plus a view-only plan with a quote button. The v2.0.0
    “roughly 1100×700px or larger” inline guardrail protected the OLD
    drag-and-drop editor and was silently downgrading every tablet and
    phone visitor to the launcher card in front of the old editor. Launcher
    and Popup modes still render the launcher card. (The actual decision
    runs inside the hosted embed.js — this plugin’s emitted snippet is
    unchanged; the note here documents the behavior change a site will see
    once the hosted app ships it.)
  • Added: a no-load fallback. If the hosted planner script never runs on a
    visitor’s browser — an office firewall or DNS filter blocking the
    planner domain, a browser extension blocking third-party scripts, or
    JavaScript off — the placement used to show literally nothing. It now
    shows a short note plus a direct “open the event planner” link to the
    hosted planner page (and the same link inside
